intended_object: The type that indexes the generators x_{ij}(a) (with i ≠ j in ι and a ∈ R) of the Steinberg presentation. It is the alphabet of the free group from which `Steinberg.Presented` is built as a quotient. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and its use in `word`, `relations` and `Presented`.
explanation:
The definition is just the product type `Root ι × R`, where `Root ι` is the subtype of pairs (i, j) with i ≠ j. Its only role is to supply the generators for `FreeGroup (Generator ι R)` and `PresentedGroup relations`. So it is an indexing device used to build the Steinberg presentation, not a mathematical object in its own right.

It does match the standard generating set {x_{ij}(a) : i ≠ j, a ∈ R} of the Steinberg group, and it uses no hypotheses on ι or R, since even the `[Ring R]` instance is introduced only afterwards. It therefore raises no faithfulness or generality issue. Mathlib has no Steinberg group, so there is no counterpart to cite.
